repro: GET https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/priest/bookings?limit=500 with the ct+pandit bearer token and header 'Accept-Language: en-GB,en;q=0.9'
expected the user-facing `message` in English — the caller asked for English and this account never chose a language
repeat the same request with '&lang=en' to see the English catalogue entry the header could not reach
findings.observed: The `message` comes back in Hindi regardless of Accept-Language. Same with no Accept-Language header at all, and reproduced on three different codes: INVALID_QUERY (/priest/bookings), FORBIDDEN (/temple-portal/dashboard) and NOT_FOUND (/priest/bookings/:id). Adding '?lang=en' DOES return 'One or more query parameters are invalid.', which proves the English catalogue is present and only the header is being ignored. Cause: signup hard-sets the language to Hindi (SIGNUP_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = 'hi', apps/api/src/lib/i18n.ts:81, applied at apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:516 and :1464; the column default at apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:178 is also hi), and pickLangFor ranks the stored value ABOVE Accept-Language (apps/api/src/lib/error-i18n.ts:377-410) on the stated reasoning that 'a profile setting is a deliberate choice' — reasoning that does not hold when the stored value is a signup default the user never saw. Net effect: Accept-Language is dead for every signed-in account and only an explicit ?lang= selects English. HONEST SCOPING — this does not reach a screen today, and I checked why rather than assuming: packages/api-client/src/error-shapes.ts:103-111 lists FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND/INVALID_BODY/INVALID_QUERY in LOCALIZER_GENERIC_CODES and prefers the English `error` label for exactly these, and on the pandit pages apps/web/lib/pandit-api.ts:54 composes a string that apps/web/lib/friendly-error.ts:182 then flattens to English copy. So this is a latent defect in the localization layer, not a visible one — it becomes user-visible the moment any client starts trusting `message`.
findings.expected: With no explicit language choice on record, Accept-Language should decide; the stored value should only outrank the header once the user has actually picked a language.
findings.evidence: HTTP 400 with Accept-Language: en-GB,en;q=0.9 — body: {"error":"Invalid query","details":{"formErrors":[],"fieldErrors":{"limit":["Number must be less than or equal to 100"]}},"message":"एक या अधिक क्वेरी पैरामीटर अमान्य हैं।","code":"INVALID_QUERY"}. Verified twice, and against ?lang=en which returns the English sentence for the same code.

blocked.target: Authenticated render of all 19 portal pages (/priest/*, /temple-portal/*)
blocked.reason: The web revives its session from the httpOnly darshya_session cookie, which the API sets host-only for api.darshya.online and only ever mints on POST /auth/login — the one endpoint the brief forbids. The token cache holds bearer tokens with no refresh token, so no browser session could be constructed by any permitted route. Pages were verified three other ways instead: logged-out HTTP (clean 307 to /auth/login for all 19), HTML past the cosmetic poojly_user middleware marker (200, sane title, no error boundary), and one live in-browser load confirming the shell resolves to the login redirect in ~3 s rather than hanging. What could NOT be observed is each list page's authenticated empty-state rendering.
